title: Swimmer Archie Goodburn Helps Win New Support for Brain Cancer Patients
summary:
Scottish swimmer Archie Goodburn has helped convince the United Kingdom's government to take new steps to improve care for people with brain cancer.

Goodburn, who is 25, was diagnosed two years ago with three brain tumors that doctors cannot remove with surgery. He went for medical tests after having health problems while training for the 2024 Olympic trials. He has been treated with medicines and radiation therapy. Even so, he kept racing and reached the final of the 50-meter breaststroke at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

After Goodburn made an emotional appeal on TV for more money for brain cancer research, Prime Minister Andy Burnham invited him to Downing Street, where the prime minister works. After their meeting, Burnham announced several plans.

The government will name a national leader for brain cancer care. It will also review how much progress has been made on brain cancer since 2018 and what is still holding progress back. The review will be led by Professor Anthony Chalmers of the University of Glasgow. After that, a national plan aims to get new treatments "out of the lab and to patients faster," the government said.

Burnham also asked the agency that oversees medicines to finish reviewing its rules for treatments for rare conditions in two years instead of three. Patients, families and charities will help design a push to get more people into clinical trials, which test new treatments.

Goodburn thanked the prime minister. He said all three of his requests had been "promised to some extent," but that the details still need work.

Burnham called Goodburn "an inspiration to us all." He said, "Families facing this disease can't afford to wait."
why_it_matters: One athlete's public appeal led to government action that could help brain cancer patients get new treatments sooner.

keywords.explanation: Tumors are lumps of cells that grow in the body when they should not.
Diagnosed means a doctor has found out what illness a person has.
Breaststroke is a swimming style where the arms push forward and sweep out while the legs kick like a frog.
Radiation therapy is a treatment that uses strong energy beams to attack cancer cells.
Clinical trials are careful tests that check whether new medical treatments are safe and work.
